column1: # Supplementary Table 2. The 383 recurrent genes scored against published pH and agonal-state gene lists, and against this study's control-pH association.

# Columns: axis; n_genes, genes in the set; n_with_sign, genes with a schizophrenia direction; n_with_value, genes with a value on the axis; mean_score, mean signed score (positive when a gene moves in schizophrenia the way it moves with low pH, or with fever or infection for Dai et al.); concordant, discordant, genes scoring positive and negative; frac_concordant; null_mean, null_sd, mean and standard deviation over 10,000 random gene sets of the same size matched on expression decile; z; p_one_sided; n_axis_genes, genes on the source's axis; source; tissue; platform; n_samples; n_samples_note; z_corrected, p_corrected_one_sided, z divided by the square root of the variance inflation factor vif (1 + (m - 1) x rho_bar, m = n_with_value, rho_bar = mean pairwise correlation of the genes in control brain expression) and its one-sided normal P.

# The last row uses the control-pH association (combined z over the ten control dataset-regions). Its variance inflation factor takes the correlation among genes from the control residuals (after pH, age and sex) of those 10 datasets, pooled with the weights and per-gene dataset membership of the statistic; the Hatano and Miyahara rows take it from the same ten dataset-regions, and the Dai row from GTEx cortex.
